Q: What are the sources of water in your school and home?

Ans: In the school and home the water comes mainly from underground water, taken out through taps, hand pumps or tube wells; rain water collected and stored is also a source. (Answers may differ from place to place — the sources named in the chapter are glaciers, rain, lakes, springs and underground water.)

Point to Ponder!

Q: How do we use underground water? Make a list from your observations in your homes, school and surrounding environment.

Ans: We take underground water out through hand pumps, wells and tube wells and use it for drinking, cooking, washing clothes and utensils, bathing and cleaning, and for watering plants. The rain water absorbed by the ground passes through many layers of the Earth, is filtered by them, and becomes clean drinkable underground water.

Point to Ponder!

Q: In fact the brick wall is made of clay. How?

Ans: Bricks are made of clay. Wet clay can be moulded into any shape, so it is moulded into the shape of bricks; when dried it retains its shape and becomes more hard. These hard clay bricks are then used to build the brick wall.

lessons.title: Short Answers and Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Artificial satellites help with radio and television transmission, internet, telephone contact, locating our position, weather prediction and navigation.
  • The Moon is a satellite of the Earth, and the Earth is a satellite of the Sun because it revolves around the Sun due to the Sun's gravity.
  • A geo-stationary satellite at about 36000 km above the equator moves with the Earth, so it appears stationary from the Earth.
  • Astronauts wear a space dress because there is no air in space; it supplies oxygen and protects their body.
  • A telescope on a satellite is above the atmosphere, so air, dust and clouds do not disturb its view and it sends clearer photographs.
  • In the gravity free environment of space, astronauts and objects float, and water cannot be poured into a glass because it floats as drops.

Solved Exercises

Q: Write the names of 5 benefits which we get from artificial satellites?

Ans: Five benefits we get from artificial satellites are: (1) Radio, television transmission and information by internet reach every part of the world. (2) We can make contact with far off places by telephone. (3) We can correctly locate our position anywhere in the world. (4) We can predict changes in weather much earlier, which helps us to deal with floods, storms, forest fires and other disasters effectively. (5) They help in precise navigation and in the exploration of the Earth resources.

Q: Moon is satellite of the Earth. Is the Earth also satellite of some bigger object? What is that object?

Ans: Yes. The Moon revolves around the Earth due to the Earth's gravity, so it is a satellite of the Earth. In the same way, the Earth revolves around the Sun due to the Sun's gravity. So the Earth is also a satellite of a bigger object, and that object is the Sun.

Q: Why does a geo-stationary satellite appear to be stationary?

Ans: A geo-stationary satellite revolves around the Earth with the same speed as that of the Earth, at a height of about 36000 km, positioned directly above the equator. Because it moves along with the Earth and completes one orbit in one day, it appears stationary at one place all the time when viewed from the Earth.

Q: Why do the astronauts wear space dress? What are its benefits?

Ans: Astronauts wear a special space dress (space suit) because there is no air in space and the conditions there are very different from the Earth. The space dress supplies them oxygen to breathe, protects their body from the harmful conditions of space and keeps them safe while they work and walk in space, for example during a space walk outside the space station.

Q: Why a telescope installed on a satellite can take more clear photographs than from the Earth surface?

Ans: A telescope installed on a satellite is above the Earth's atmosphere, so its view is not blocked or disturbed by the air, dust and clouds of the atmosphere. Therefore it can observe space and send us much clearer photographs and information than a telescope working from the Earth surface.

Q: What provides the force needed to keep artificial satellites moving around the Earth? Indicate its direction on the two satellites shown in the given figure.

Ans: Diagram (in words): The Earth is shown in the centre, with two artificial satellites on a dotted oval orbit around it — one satellite on the left side of the Earth and one at the upper right of the orbit — and arrows on the orbit showing the direction of movement of the satellites. The force that keeps the satellites moving around the Earth is the gravity of the Earth. Its direction on both satellites is towards the centre of the Earth, i.e. from each satellite straight inward towards the Earth.

Q: Astronauts have to face a lot of problems in space. Can you name some of these problems?

Ans: Astronauts face many problems in space. There is no air in space, so they cannot breathe without special arrangements. The space station has a gravity free environment, so they and everything around them float, which makes eating, drinking, moving and working difficult. They have to stay in the space station for several months, away from the Earth, and they need space shuttles to go to the station and come back from it.

Q: How do the astronauts respire in your opinion?

Ans: There is no air in space, so astronauts cannot breathe directly. In my opinion, they respire with the help of oxygen supplied to them. Inside the space station and the space shuttle, air with oxygen is provided for breathing, and when they go out for a space walk, oxygen is supplied through their space dress.

Q: Why cannot you pour water in a glass in space?

Ans: We cannot pour water in a glass in space because space has a gravity free environment. On the Earth, water falls down into the glass due to gravity, but in space there is no gravity to pull the water down, so the water does not flow down and instead floats about in the form of drops.

The Russian Space Station MIR also orbited the Earth for 15 years at a height of 300 km and scientists performed many fascinating experiments in it.

Q: Find out from the library or internet, the first five astronauts who visited the space. From which country do they belong? What were dates of their missions and how long did they stay in space?

Ans: The first five astronauts who visited space were: (1) Yuri Gagarin of the Soviet Union — April 12, 1961 — the first human to enter space and return safely, staying about 108 minutes. (2) Alan Shepard of America — May 5, 1961 — stayed about 15 minutes. (3) Virgil Grissom of America — July 21, 1961 — stayed about 15 minutes. (4) Gherman Titov of the Soviet Union — August 6, 1961 — stayed about one day (25 hours). (5) John Glenn of America — February 20, 1962 — stayed about 5 hours. The chapter itself names the first of them: Soviet Cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human to enter space and return safely on April 12, 1961.

lessons.title: Short Answers and Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A model foot bridge needs skewers, ice-cream sticks, paper, thread and glue; the design is first sketched on paper.
  • A spirit level checks a horizontal surface, while a plumb line checks a vertical surface or wall.
  • An LED is a tiny light-emitting bulb; it glows at 2 to 3 volts, its longer leg is positive (+) and its shorter leg is negative (-).
  • A picture frame is horizontal when the spirit-level bubble is exactly in the middle, and vertical when it is parallel to the hanging plumb line.
  • First aid is temporary care for sudden illness or injury, e.g. dressing a wound to prevent infection before shifting the person to hospital.
  • A wooden model needs tools such as skewers, ice-cream sticks, cardboard, paper, thread, glue, scissors, a cutter and pliers, used carefully under a teacher's supervision.
  • A musical instrument produces sound by the vibration of its stretched parts, and in an LED light string all long (positive) legs are joined together and all short (negative) legs together.

Solved Exercises

Q: What do you need to make a model of foot bridge?

Ans: To make a model of a foot bridge we need skewers, ice cream sticks, paper, thread and glue. A skewer is a long thin pointed piece of wood or metal. The design is first sketched on paper, the skewers are cut to size, two side walls with triangles are made and joined with thread and glue, the deck is made by pasting ice-cream sticks on a strip of paper, and the deck is fixed on the beams between the two side walls.

Q: What is difference between the functions of spirit level and plumb line?

Ans: A spirit level is used to check whether a surface is horizontal or not, while a plumb line is used to check whether a surface or wall is vertical or not. The mason uses a plumb line to keep a wall vertically straight, and the spirit level is used by carpenters, masons and others to level horizontal surfaces such as a table top.

Q: What is an LED?

Ans: LEDs are the tiny light emitting bulbs. When a small voltage of 2 to 3 volts is applied across an LED, it starts glowing. Lights of different colours are emitted by different LEDs. The longer leg (wire) of an LED is positive (+) and the shorter one is negative (-).

Q: You have to install a picture frame on the wall. How it can be kept straight horizontally as well as vertically?

Ans: To keep a picture frame straight horizontally, a spirit level is placed on it: if the bubble is exactly in the middle of the two marked lines on the tube, the frame is perfectly horizontal. To keep it straight vertically, a plumb line is used: the frame is vertical when it is parallel to the hanging plumb line and the bob just touches along its side.

Q: What is meant by first aid?

Ans: First aid is a temporary care given to a person who has got sudden illness or injury. For example, a wound is dressed with the help of a first aid box to prevent it from infection, and then the injured person is shifted to hospital for proper treatment.

Q: What sort of tools and equipments are required to make a wooden model?

Ans: To make a wooden model, tools and equipment such as skewers (long thin pointed pieces of wood), ice cream sticks, card board, paper, thread, glue, scissors, a cutter, pliers, packing tape and coloured paper are required, as used in the model making activities of this chapter. The work should be done carefully under the supervision of the teacher, keeping the area clean and putting sharp tools at their proper place after use.

Q: How does a musical instrument produce sound?

Ans: A musical instrument produces sound by the vibration of its stretched parts. In the simple guitar made in this chapter, two rubber bands are stretched on a shoe box on one side and two more on the other side of the tube, and pencils are inserted under them to make their lengths effectively different. When the rubber bands are plucked with a finger, they vibrate and produce low and loud tones.

Q: Why is it necessary to join long wires of LEDs together and short wires together while preparing a light string?

Ans: The longer leg (wire) of an LED is positive (+) and the shorter leg is negative (-). While preparing a light string, all the positive legs must be at one side and all the negative legs at the other side, and the positive legs are joined together and the negative legs are joined together, so that every LED is connected with the correct polarity to the battery. If an LED is joined the wrong way, it will not glow; then its leg sides have to be changed and checked again.

mcqs.q: Why are long wires of LEDs joined together and short wires together in a light string?
options: So every LED is connected with the correct polarity to the battery
So the string becomes longer only
mcqs.why: The longer leg is positive and the shorter is negative. Joining long legs together and short legs together keeps every LED at the correct polarity; an LED joined the wrong way will not glow.

Investigate and Project Work

Q: You are provided 6 volt battery, one strip of cardboard and 12 blue colour LEDs. How will you make a decorating light?

Ans: Following the method of Activity 10.5: Take the strip of cardboard and make pairs of holes in it at equal distances with the help of a steel nail. Insert all the 12 blue LEDs in the holes, keeping the positive legs (longer wires) at one side of the strip and the shorter negative legs at the other side. Join the positive legs of each small set together and their negative legs together, then join the sets with each other (negative side of one set to the positive side of the next set), because one LED needs only 2 to 3 volts and the battery is of 6 volts. Finally connect the positive side to the positive terminal of the 6 volt battery and the negative side to the negative terminal. The LEDs will start glowing and the decorating light will be ready. Never connect this LED string to 220 V A.C.

Q: Make a model of stretcher with low cost material.

Ans: A model of a stretcher can be made with low cost material by taking two long strong sticks or bamboo poles and fixing a strong piece of cloth, an old sheet or sacking firmly between them, tied or stitched along both poles. The two poles act as handles and the cloth in the middle carries the injured person, so that the person can be supported and shifted safely to a safe place or to an ambulance, as practised in shifting a person to hospital.
